Temperature Controlled Storage and Distribution (TCS&D)
The magazine’s title, spells the editorial policy firmly guided by what suppliers and end users of temperature controlled business need to know for more cost effective operations.
Quality and relevance are the top priorities in selection and use of all editorial material. The central editorial theme is the perishable product supply chain, but space is also reserved for other applications of temperature and environment control that may benefit our readers. Through the magazine’s editorial pages, you can come face-to-face every month with people, companies, operations, developments in the industry to help your own business plans. This continuity of dialogue is our chief objective!
Readers are drawn from a wide spectrum – Food Manufacturers, wholesalers, independent and multiple retailers, caterers, importers, exporters – all who either provide their added value logistical services – cold and chill storage, primary and local distribution, truck and trailer rental, inter – and multi-modal operations by road, rail, sea and air.
Their suppliers – cold store and food facility contractors, insulated panel refrigeration supply/installation companies, insulated trailer and rigid body builders, materials handling equipment, transport refrigeration sales and services companies, in vehicle air conditioning, suppliers or temperature monitors & recording equipment, satellite tracking …
All the many companies and individuals in fact, whose activities are linked with the perishable food supply chain.
TCS&D magazine – the tried and tested impartial magazine.

Noble Foods Partners with Starfrost to Launch Value-Added Convenience Food Products Using High Performance Freezing Technology
The pre-prepared foods market is experiencing rapid growth, driven by consumer demand for quick, nutritious meals. Recognising this shift, Noble Foods—best known for its flagship brand, the happy egg co.—has partnered with Starfrost, a leading innovator in cooling technology, to launch a new range of value-added, ready-to-cook omelettes.
Central to this collaboration are two of Starfrost’s state-of-the-art Helix Spiral Freezers, which are enabling Noble Foods to launch a new production line efficiently while maintaining the highest standards of product quality and consistency.
Noble Foods is known for its popular brand, the happy egg co. Can you tell us about your new venture and why you decided to move into the value-added convenience sector?
Moving into the pre-prepared food space was a natural progression.
What led you to choose Starfrost’s Helix Spiral Freezer, and how did you select the right solution?
We knew we needed a system that would give us flexibility, reliability and efficiency.
We found Starfrost to be a trusted name in the industry.
Their equipment stood out for its durability, ease of use and the company’s commitment to long-term relationships and aftercare.
That was crucial for us.
You explored liquid nitrogen freezing—why did you ultimately opt for mechanical freezing?
Cryogenic freezing comes with volatile pricing and complex transport considerations, whereas mechanical freezing offered more stability and lower long-term costs.
How has the spiral freezer benefited you in terms of consistency and production scalability?
The freezing process is extremely reliable, which ensures our product quality remains high.
From an engineering standpoint, the system is intuitive and straightforward to operate, and it performs well under different production conditions.
What’s next for Noble Foods and the happy egg co. brand?
As our business grows, we’ll need equipment that evolves with us.
Starfrost’s freezer systems provide that scalability.
The Helix Spiral Freezer is future-proof—designed to handle greater capacity and accommodate alternative products as production ramps up.
Starfrost’s Helix Spiral Freezers provide Noble Foods with the capacity, consistency, and flexibility required to scale and diversify, enabling the food manufacturer to meet growing demand—efficiently and reliably.
